title: Dispatch: in-band record-relationship manifest (attempt 1)
description:
PARENT SPEC: eshyra-o9bd.19.1.4 (run `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.1.4` and read the
2026-09-12 DESIGN SESSION note in full before writing code). Authority: ADR 0020
(sections 1, 3, 4, 8), docs/design/evidence-trust-model.md, docs/importer-fix-protocol.md,
AGENTS.md. This child delivers DELIVERABLE 1 only. Deliverable 2 (the capability
ledger) is a sibling child and is NOT yours - do not touch
discovery/packet.ts, discovery/signals.ts, state/itemExecutionReadiness.ts, or
scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/.

WORKTREE: .worktrees/eshyra-z7bm on branch eshyra-z7bm
(already created for you, cut from branch eshyra-o9bd.19.1.4). Run
`cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` first and work only from there.
Run `npm ci` in the worktree before verifying.

=== THE DEFECT (measured; reproduce it before you fix it) ===
packages/core/src/discovery/expansion.ts::directLinks hardcodes a consumer-side
allowlist of traversable fields and a per-field target-resolution mode:
  data.source, data.parentClass, data.progressionTableRef,
  data.tableRefs[], data.spellTableRefs[], data.statBlockRefs[],
  data.mechanics.conditions[].condition (resolved by normalized NAME, not key).
The field NAME does not determine the meaning. Over the shipped pack
(packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, 1812 records):
  feature   /source  n=184 resolved=184  value is a record key ("class:barbarian")
  ancestry  /source  n=13  resolved=0    value is the literal label "race" - a
                                         source SECTION name, not a record key
  subclass /parentClass 12/12 | class /progressionTableRef 12/12
  rule /tableRefs 38/38 | magic-item /tableRefs 32/32 | magic-item /statBlockRefs 2/2
  spell /tableRefs 9/9 | feature /tableRefs 4/4 | background /tableRefs 4/4
  subclass /spellTableRefs 10/10 | mechanics.conditions 195 refs, 0 unresolved
The importer already knows the difference and records it as human prose in
packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/fieldProvenanceDeclarations.ts:
  ancestry '/source' -> "a structural field describing where this ancestry sits in
                         the source (page/section), not narrative prose."
  feature  '/source' -> "the granting class/subclass record-key, not source text."
No consumer can act on prose, so expansion applies one meaning to both kinds and
silently drops all 13 ancestry values: directLinks' inner add() returns early when
the key does not resolve. "not a reference", "target absent" and "found nothing"
become indistinguishable - recurring fail-open idiom 1 of eshyra-o9bd.19.7 and the
behaviour ADR 0020 section 3 forbids.

=== REQUIRED INVARIANT ===
A runtime consumer obtains a record's declared relationships from pack-owned data,
and every non-resolution is a distinguishable typed outcome, never a silent drop.

=== BUILD THIS ===
1. NEW packages/core/src/rules/recordRelationships.ts.
   Model it CLOSELY on packages/core/src/rules/fieldProvenance.ts - same module
   doc-comment style (state what the module replaces and WHY a default is
   forbidden), same (kind, pointerPrefix) declaration model with every array index
   collapsed to the literal segment '*', same longest-prefix-wins matching, same
   "an unmatched lookup returns undefined, never a default" rule.
     export type RelationshipDisposition = 'reference' | 'not-a-reference';
     export type RelationshipTargetResolution = 'record-key' | 'record-name';
     export interface RecordRelationshipDeclaration {
       kind: RulesRecordKind; pointerPrefix: string;
       disposition: RelationshipDisposition;
       relation?: string;                       // required iff disposition==='reference'
       targetResolution?: RelationshipTargetResolution;  // same
       targetKind?: RulesRecordKind;            // required iff targetResolution==='record-name'
       reason: string;                          // required, non-empty, reviewable evidence
     }
     export const RECORD_RELATIONSHIP_SCHEMA = 'record-relationships-v1';
     export interface RecordRelationshipManifest { schema: ...; declarations: readonly ... }
     export function buildRecordRelationshipManifest(decls): RecordRelationshipManifest
   'not-a-reference' is the load-bearing half: ancestry '/source' is DECLARED not a
   reference, with its reason, so "declared not to be a link" is distinguishable
   from "nobody classified it". Reject a declaration whose optional fields
   contradict its disposition (a 'not-a-reference' carrying a relation, a
   'reference' missing targetResolution, a 'record-name' missing targetKind), a
   malformed/empty pointerPrefix, an unknown kind, and duplicate
   (kind, pointerPrefix) pairs - all throw a RecordRelationshipError extending
   RulesPackError, exactly as buildFieldProvenanceManifest does.
2. Resolution returns a DISCRIMINATED UNION per value. Never a filtered array.
     export type RelationshipResolution =
       | { outcome: 'resolved'; sourceRecordKey; pointer; relation; targetRecordKey; declaration }
       | { outcome: 'unresolved-target'; sourceRecordKey; pointer; relation; rawValue;
           reason: 'no-record-with-key' | 'no-record-with-name' | 'ambiguous-name'; declaration };
   export function resolveRecordRelationships(manifest, record, index) walks the
   record's real data leaves with the same walker fieldProvenance.ts uses
   (walkFieldPointers - reuse it, do not write a second walker), and for each leaf
   whose pointer matches a 'reference' declaration, resolves the target. An
   unresolved target is RETAINED in the output as 'unresolved-target'. A leaf
   matching a 'not-a-reference' declaration contributes nothing and is not an
   error. A leaf matching NO declaration contributes nothing and makes no claim -
   the manifest's claim is bounded to what it declares; do not invent a
   corpus-wide coverage gate over RulesRecord.data (ADR 0020 rejects that global
   negative explicitly).
3. FAIL-CLOSED GATE over a bounded, independently justified population.
   export function assertRecordRelationshipDeclarationsAreLive(records, manifest):
   every declaration must match at least one real leaf pointer in the emitted
   record set, or the build fails naming the dead declaration. This catches typos
   and drift. Its population is the declaration list itself, which is finite and
   reviewed - not a claim about the corpus.
4. CURATED COMPILER INPUT: NEW
   packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/recordRelationshipDeclarations.ts,
   sibling in shape and documentation style to fieldProvenanceDeclarations.ts. It
   is an ADR 0017 section 3 curated input, not generated output. Seed it with
   EXACTLY the eleven measured (kind, pointerPrefix) pairs listed in THE DEFECT
   above plus the ancestry '/source' not-a-reference row - that migration
   denominator comes from the DELETED consumer allowlist, not from the pack under
   repair, which is what makes it independently justified. Give each row a reason
   grounded in what the parser actually emits; where fieldProvenanceDeclarations.ts
   already states the reason, quote it.
   Pick relation names that read as DISCOVERY REASONS (ADR 0020 section 4:
   relationships are retrieval reasons, never exclusive ownership). Suggested, but
   use your judgement and justify in the reason text: 'granted-by' (feature
   /source), 'parent-class' (subclass /parentClass), 'progression-table'
   (class /progressionTableRef), 'table-reference' (the *tableRefs families),
   'stat-block-reference' (magic-item /statBlockRefs). For
   /mechanics/conditions/*/condition keep the EXISTING per-entry relation
   vocabulary (rules/conditionRelations.ts CONDITION_RELATION_VALUES) - that
   relation is carried by the DATA, not by the declaration, so declare it as a
   'record-name' reference to targetKind 'condition' and let the resolver read the
   per-entry relation from the record. Preserve today's behaviour that an entry
   whose relation is not in CONDITION_RELATION_VALUES is skipped, and state in the
   reason why that is a data-validity skip rather than a fail-open.
5. EMIT + LOAD, mirroring field-provenance.json end to end:
   - scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/emit.ts: build the manifest once, run the
     live-declaration gate over the FINAL validated records before writing
     anything, and write record-relationships.json unconditionally beside
     field-provenance.json.
   - packages/core/src/rules/packLoader.ts: PACK_RECORD_RELATIONSHIPS_FILE +
     loadRecordRelationshipManifest(dir), optional like the provenance one, with
     the module doc comment updated to describe the new artifact.
   - packages/core/src/rules/bundledSrdPack.ts:
     getBundledDnd5eSrdRecordRelationshipManifest(), lazily loaded, cached and
     deep-frozen exactly as the provenance one is.
6. REPLACE THE CONSUMER HEURISTIC. Delete directLinks from
   packages/core/src/discovery/expansion.ts and drive expansion from the manifest,
   threaded in by discovery/harness.ts the same way the field-provenance manifest
   already is (see harness.ts's bundledDnd5eSrdFieldProvenanceSource comment and
   mirror its reasoning). Keep TypedTraversal's existing shape and the existing
   dedup/route/band behaviour for resolved links - this is a substitution of the
   SOURCE OF TRUTH, not a redesign of expansion. Surface unresolved-target
   outcomes on the ExpansionTrace so they are visible evidence; do not drop them
   and do not turn them into routes.
   A pack with NO manifest declares no relationships and must SAY SO (an explicit
   manifest-absent note on the trace). It must NOT fall back to the old allowlist.
   Existing discovery tests that build hand-made packs may need a manifest; give
   them one rather than reinstating a default.

=== REGRESSION PREDICATE (assert IDENTITIES, never counts) ===
R1 THE DISCRIMINATING CONTROL: from the same field name '/source',
   feature:barbarian:ability-score-improvement resolves to class:barbarian as a
   'reference', while ancestry:dwarf resolves to the 'not-a-reference' declaration,
   produces no traversal, and is not a silent drop. The old code fails this.
R2 A declaration naming a pointer no record emits fails
   assertRecordRelationshipDeclarationsAreLive, naming it.
R3 A 'record-key' reference whose value names an absent key yields
   {outcome:'unresolved-target', reason:'no-record-with-key'} and appears on the
   expansion trace. A 'record-name' reference matching no condition yields
   'no-record-with-name'; one matching several yields 'ambiguous-name'.
R4 Manifest construction throws on: empty pointerPrefix, a prefix not starting with
   '/', a duplicate (kind, pointerPrefix), an unknown kind, a 'not-a-reference'
   carrying a relation, a 'reference' without targetResolution, a 'record-name'
   without targetKind, an empty reason.
R5 Expansion over a pack with no manifest yields zero traversals AND a
   manifest-absent note - it never silently behaves like the old allowlist.
R6 The existing expansion behaviour is preserved for the ten resolving families:
   pin the exact resolved (sourceRecordKey, relation, targetRecordKey) identities
   for at least one real record in each, so a silent regression in any one family
   fails. Do not assert a total count as the predicate.

=== VERIFICATION ===
- npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing (it rewrites files).
- Regenerate the pack through the importer and run npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack;
  records.json must NOT change (the new artifact is a sibling file). If
  records.json changes, STOP and report - that is outside this fix.
- Report in your completion notes: generated files added/changed, why each is
  expected, exact commands run and results, and the before/after for the ancestry
  and feature '/source' cases.

=== PROHIBITIONS ===
No alias, topic, or canonical-identity CONTENT (that is eshyra-o9bd.19.2.4).
No corpus-wide relationship inventory, coverage claim, or gate over
RulesRecord.data. No second walker. No default disposition anywhere. No hand-edit
of records.json. No change to capability code. Do not weaken an existing test or
audit expectation to make this pass - see docs/importer-fix-protocol.md.

If the failure map reveals a new root cause, requires a new parser or extractor
strategy, or creates generated churn outside the direct consequences of this
minimal fix, stop and report instead of broadening the implementation.

=== REVIEW REPAIR ROUND 1 (supervisor, 2026-09-12). NOT ACCEPTED. Repair on this
same branch (eshyra-z7bm) as additional commits; do not start over. ===

Your implementation's core is sound and survives: the (kind, pointerPrefix) declaration
model, longest-prefix-wins matching, reuse of walkFieldPointers, the contradiction checks
in buildRecordRelationshipManifest, the curated declarations file, the emitted
record-relationships.json sibling artifact, the loader and bundled-accessor wiring, and
records.json = 0 changes. Fix the following and nothing else.

F1 BLOCKING - NO REGRESSION COVERAGE EXISTS. You added zero new test files. `git diff
   --stat` over packages/core/test/ shows only signature fixes so existing tests compile.
   Every predicate R1-R6 in this bead's spec is missing. Implement ALL of them as real
   tests, in a new packages/core/test/ file (recordRelationships.test.ts, plus discovery
   assertions where the predicate is about expansion). R1 is the one that matters most and
   must be written so it FAILS against the pre-fix behaviour: from the SAME field name
   '/source', feature:barbarian:ability-score-improvement resolves to class:barbarian with
   relation 'granted-by', while ancestry:dwarf matches the not-a-reference declaration,
   produces no traversal, and is not a silent drop. Assert IDENTITIES, never counts.

F2 BLOCKING - the manifest is an OPTIONAL option that silently defaults to "no
   relationships". expandTypedRelationships(candidates, stack) with
   options.relationshipManifest omitted returns zero traversals, so any call site you did
   not update degrades silently and the compiler cannot catch it. That is the fail-open
   idiom this bead exists to remove: a missing input producing an empty successful result.
   Make the manifest a REQUIRED parameter so omission is a compile error. A pack that
   genuinely declares no relationships passes an empty manifest explicitly.

F3 BLOCKING - traversalOf() re-derives linkField from the pointer with a string hack,
   including the hardcoded special case
     pointer === '/mechanics/conditions/*/condition' ? 'data.mechanics.conditions' : ...
     and `.replaceAll('/', '.')`.
   That reintroduces exactly the consumer-side string heuristic this bead deletes, and it
   is load-bearing: route triggers are `${linkField}:${relation}`, so dedup and route
   identity depend on it. Carry linkField on the declaration (a declared field, reviewed
   like every other) or carry the declaration identity on TypedTraversal. Do not re-derive
   it from the pointer.

F4 BLOCKING - conditionRelation() resolves the relation BY CONDITION NAME, returning the
   first mechanics.conditions entry whose condition matches, because walkFieldPointers
   collapses the array index to '*' and the real index is lost. If a record ever lists the
   same condition twice with different relations, every occurrence takes the first entry's
   relation. The code you replaced was structurally immune - it iterated entries and read
   each entry's own relation. I checked the shipped pack: 0 records exhibit this today, so
   it is latent, not active. Shipping a mechanism that is only accidentally correct is the
   failure mode this whole program exists to stop. Resolve the relation per ENTRY, not per
   name, and add a test with a synthetic record listing one condition twice with two
   different relations proving each occurrence keeps its own.

F5 'relationship-manifest-absent' is pushed as a candidate LOSS. A missing manifest is a
   configuration fact, not a candidate the stage lost, and losses feed
   measurements.ts:492's perStage.losses count with a defined meaning (design section
   13.3). Carry it as its own field on ExpansionTrace instead.

F6 The unresolved-target detail uses a double cast (`resolution as unknown as
   Record<string, unknown>`). Give StageLoss detail (or the new trace field) a shape that
   does not need it.

Re-run npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing. Re-run the importer and
npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack if anything you change affects emission; records.json must
still show 0 changes. Append a completion report to this bead stating, per finding, what
you changed and which test now proves it, then close this bead again.
